references.text: The people also quarreled with Moses at Rephidim over water, a similar rebellion against Moses due to lack of water.
The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron and wished they had died in Egypt, the same type of complaint and wish for death.
The reference to 'when our brothers died before the Lord' points to Korah's rebellion where many Israelites perished.
The people complained to the Lord's ears, another example of Israel's repeated grumbling in the wilderness.
The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the Desert of Sin and wished they had died in Egypt, a similar complaint and wish for death.
The psalm describes the incident at the waters of Meribah where the people made Moses angry, a poetic reflection on this event.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did and were killed, a New Testament reference to Israel's rebellion in the wilderness.
